units.title: Osnove
units.theme: Everyday greetings, self-introduction, numbers, colors, and family vocabulary for absolute beginners.

skills.title: Pozdravi
skills.grammarFocus: Bosnian distinguishes informal address (ti) from formal or plural address (vi): 'Kako si?' (asking one person you're informal with) vs 'Kako ste?' (formal, or speaking to more than one person).

skills.title: Predstavljanje
skills.grammarFocus: Present tense of 'biti' (to be): ja sam, ti si, on/ona/ono je, mi smo, vi ste, oni/one su.

skills.title: Brojevi 1-10
skills.grammarFocus: Bosnian numbers change the case of the noun that follows: 'jedan' (one) agrees in gender with the noun; 2-4 take the noun in genitive singular ('dva stola' - two tables); 5 and above take the noun in genitive plural ('pet stolova' - five tables).

skills.title: Boje
skills.grammarFocus: Bosnian adjectives — including colors — agree in gender with the noun they describe: 'crven auto' (red car, masculine), 'crvena jabuka' (red apple, feminine), 'crveno cvijeće' (red flowers, neuter).

skills.title: Porodica
skills.grammarFocus: Possessive pronouns agree in gender with the noun they modify: 'moj brat' (my brother, masculine), 'moja sestra' (my sister, feminine), 'moje dijete' (my child, neuter).

units.title: Svakodnevni život
units.theme: Daily routines, food and drink, shopping for everyday items, and talking about weather and the days of the week.

skills.title: Dnevna rutina
skills.grammarFocus: Reflexive verbs with 'se' (buditi se, oblačiti se, odmarati se) and the present tense of everyday verbs.

skills.title: Hrana i piće
skills.grammarFocus: The accusative case for direct objects with 'jesti' (to eat) and 'piti' (to drink), e.g. Pijem vodu, Jedem hljeb.

skills.title: Kupovina
skills.grammarFocus: Prices and quantities, asking 'Koliko košta?', and the genitive case after numbers and quantity words.

skills.title: Vrijeme i dani
skills.grammarFocus: Days of the week with 'u' + accusative, and fixed adverbial weather expressions with 'Vani je...'.

units.title: Grad i kretanje
units.theme: Giving and following directions, using public transport, talking about the past, and describing hobbies and free-time activities.

skills.title: Upute i pravci
skills.grammarFocus: The imperative (skreni, skrenite) and prepositions of place governing the genitive case (iza, pored, blizu, između).

skills.title: Prijevoz
skills.grammarFocus: The locative case with 'u' and 'na' to express where you are or how you travel, e.g. u autobusu, na stanici.

skills.title: Prošlo vrijeme
skills.grammarFocus: The perfekt tense: 'biti' + the gendered l-participle, e.g. radio sam / radila sam, išao sam / išla sam.

skills.title: Slobodno vrijeme
skills.grammarFocus: 'Voljeti' + infinitive for activities versus 'voljeti' + accusative noun for things, e.g. Volim plivati vs. Volim muziku.

units.title: Posao i obrazovanje
units.theme: Workplace and career vocabulary with the dative case, school and university life with relative clauses, health and the doctor's office with modal verbs, and expressing and defending opinions with subordinate clauses.

skills.title: Posao
skills.grammarFocus: The dative case marks the indirect object and follows verbs like reći, dati, pomoći, and pisati: masculine nouns add -u (šef → šefu), nouns ending in -a like kolega/kolegica change to -i (kolega → kolegi, kolegica → kolegici), and neuter nouns add -u (dijete → djetetu).

skills.title: Obrazovanje
skills.grammarFocus: The relative pronoun koji (who/which) agrees in gender and number with the noun it refers to, but its case depends on its role inside the clause: 'Profesor koji predaje historiju' (nominative) vs. 'Fakultet na kojem studiram' (locative).

skills.title: Zdravlje
skills.grammarFocus: Trebati, morati, and moći are the three core modal verbs: morati expresses strict obligation, moći expresses ability or permission, and trebati expresses need and can be personal or impersonal with the dative ('treba mi lijek').

skills.title: Mišljenja
skills.grammarFocus: Opinions are stated with mislim da / smatram da (I think/believe that) followed by a full subordinate clause with its own subject and verb; agreement and disagreement use slažem se / ne slažem se sa + instrumental.

units.title: Putovanja i mediji
units.theme: Travel bookings and directions abroad with the future tense, internet and news vocabulary with comparatives and superlatives, future intentions and plans, and real versus hypothetical conditional sentences.

skills.title: Putovanja
skills.grammarFocus: The future tense combines clitic forms of htjeti (ću, ćeš, će, ćemo, ćete, će) with the infinitive, either as two words ('Ja ću putovati') or merged ('putovaću'); the clitic cannot open a sentence, and negation is a single word (neću, nećeš…) that never merges.

skills.title: Mediji i tehnologija
skills.grammarFocus: Comparatives are usually formed by adding -iji/-ji/-eći to the adjective stem (brz → brži) and are followed by od + noun to mean 'than'; superlatives add naj- to the comparative (brži → najbrži), with irregulars like dobar → bolji → najbolji.

skills.title: Planovi i budućnost
skills.grammarFocus: Namjeravati and planirati (+ infinitive) express intentions and plans; after temporal conjunctions like kad/čim pointing to a future event, Bosnian keeps the subordinate verb in the present tense rather than the future ('Kad završim školu, naći ću posao').

skills.title: Uslovne rečenice
skills.grammarFocus: Real conditions use ako + present tense in both clauses, often with a future main clause ('Ako imam vremena, doći ću'); unreal/hypothetical conditions use the conditional mood (bih/bi + l-participle) in both clauses, typically introduced by kad bi(h).

units.title: Društvo i kultura
units.theme: Upper-intermediate discussion of social issues, environmental challenges, arts and culture, and national history and tradition — building nuanced vocabulary, subordinate clauses, verbal aspect, and passive constructions.

skills.title: Društvo
skills.grammarFocus: Complex sentences with subordinating conjunctions ('iako', 'budući da', 's obzirom na to da') and nominalization of verbs into abstract nouns for formal register.

skills.title: Okoliš
skills.grammarFocus: The se-passive construction used to describe processes and general facts without naming an agent (e.g. 'Šume se sijeku', 'Otpad se reciklira').

skills.title: Kultura i umjetnost
skills.grammarFocus: Verbal aspect (svršeni/nesvršeni glagoli) distinguishes completed vs ongoing/repeated actions, crucial when talking about creative processes and cultural events.

skills.title: Historija i tradicija
skills.grammarFocus: Awareness of the literary past tenses (aorist and imperfekt) used in storytelling, folk tales, and historical narration, alongside the everyday perfekt.

units.title: Apstraktne teme
units.theme: Abstract and opinion-based discourse spanning politics and economy, emotions and relationships, hypothetical wishes, and everyday idioms — reinforcing formal connectors, reflexive/reciprocal verbs, the conditional mood, and fixed expressions.

skills.title: Politika i ekonomija
skills.grammarFocus: Formal register and cohesive connectors ('dakle', 'stoga', 's druge strane', 'međutim') used to structure argumentative discourse on current affairs.

skills.title: Emocije i odnosi
skills.grammarFocus: Reflexive and reciprocal verbs with 'se' express emotional states and mutual relationships ('osjećati se', 'zaljubiti se', 'razumjeti se', 'svađati se').

skills.title: Izražavanje želja
skills.grammarFocus: Conditional mood (bih, bi, bi, bismo, biste, bi) for hypotheticals, and da-clauses for wishes and purpose ('želim da' / 'volio bih da').

skills.title: Idiomi i izrazi
skills.grammarFocus: Fixed idiomatic expressions whose meaning cannot be derived from individual words — mastering them is a hallmark of near-native fluency.
